walkthroughs.body_html:
There's verbal irony (saying the opposite), situational irony (the outcome is unexpected) and dramatic irony (the audience knows more than the character).

Birling calling the Titanic "unsinkable" is dramatic irony.

Sibilance creates intimacy or menace; anaphora builds rhythm and urgency.

Naming these precisely beats writing "repetition" — and examiners notice.

Zoomorphism turns humans into animals — Macbeth becomes a hunted beast.

Bathos drops the tone suddenly. Adding these to your toolkit signals real expertise.
